Rapid kinetics reduce the overall cycle duration and can improve CO 2 productivity of a DAC facility. Susteon’s sorbent design framework, outlined in Figure 1, was comprised of a hydrophobic polymer backbone to minimize water adsorption by the bulk sorbent, a highly stable proprietary amine, and a promoter to enhance CO adsorption rate. It is well understood that amines rapidly degrade at relevant 2 process conditions; thus, current research explores amine modification to improve sorbent performance. Susteon’s approach introduces an additional functional group via a promoter to the parent amine- functionalized backbone to provide stability while maintaining favorable adsorption kinetics. During this Task, sorbent optimization focused on screening functional amines and promoters to achieve high CO 2 adsorption rates and capacity as well as high oxidative stability, as oxidation is the most common mechanism of degradation for amine-based sorbents. Figure 1. Sorbent design framework High-Capacity Sorbent Development Susteon developed and used two in-house fixed bed reactors for sorbent screening and sorbent performance measurements. Figure 2 depicts a general configuration of the screening reactors. These systems can simulate a wide range of DAC operating conditions. A blended air cylinders to provide a range of CO feed 2 concentrations. An impinger mixed with dry gas feed provides humidified air feed conditions from 0% to 100% relative humidity. The sorbent sample can be regenerated using external heating jackets or directly using Joule-heating. An electric cooling jacket is also placed around the reactor to simulate sub-ambient operating temperatures. The reactor cell is interchangeable to test a range for sorbent form factors. For sorbent screening under normal operating conditions, the material is cycled between adsorption, purge, and desorption steps by adjusting the flow of gas and the sample temperature. Downstream, the gas is cooled to 2°C, allowing excess water vapor to condense before the gas flows into a non-dispersive infrared (NDIR) gas analyzer that continuously measures ppm-levels of CO in the reactor exhaust throughout the 2 experiment. Certified air is used for baseline screening and performance comparisons, and real air is used for aging tests to conserve bottled air. Granular sorbent samples with primary amine sites grafted onto a hydrophobic polymer backbone were synthesized and modified with different promoters. The promoters included amino acid surface species that were introduced via impregnation of the bulk material and alkyl groups that were incorporated via site- specific amine functionalization. The key performance metrics in the screening phase were equilibrium capacity and short-term stability (i.e., maintaining baseline capacity over 10 cycles).
